key_insight: Foundational r2SCAN-trained MLIPs can replace extra DFT correction steps and, when used as latent-feature inputs for delta-learning, substantially improve formation energies toward experimental accuracy.
engineering_relevance: This provides a more reproducible and lower-cost workflow for screening thermodynamic stability in materials databases and accelerating computational materials discovery.
method: Evaluate MC3D formation energies against OQMD, Materials Project, and experimental enthalpies
Use PET-OMATPES (r2SCAN-trained foundational MLIP) to refine formation energies without additional DFT
Train delta-learning models on MLIP latent features to further correct energies
evidence_signal: Across the evaluated databases, MLIP-based correction reduced formation-energy MAE by more than 40% versus GGA, and latent-feature delta-learning pushed error below 50 meV/atom.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality and domain coverage of the foundational MLIP and may not generalize equally well to chemistries or structures far from the training distribution.
paper_title: Correcting DFT formation energies towards experimental accuracy using foundational MLIPs and latent-feature delta-learning
